title: Iorwerth's Funny Maps and the Lost Sea Glass
markdown:
Whisperwind Creek was a town of leaning houses and giggling rivers. Everyone knew where they were going, except those using Iorwerth Buttercup's maps. Iorwerth, the town mapmaker, filled his charts with funny, helpful notes. Next to a gnarled tree: "Good for leaning. Squirrels might borrow your hat." Near the bakery: "Smells like happiness. Warning: May cause singing, even if you're tone-deaf. Embrace it!"

One crisp autumn morning, Tobin the mole, polishing his spectacles, bumped into Nell the fox. Nell was studying Iorwerth's newest map.

"Good heavens, Nell!" squeaked Tobin. "'The path forks, like a badger's opinion on hedgehogs — entirely divided and surprisingly loud.'"

Nell chuckled. "Iorwerth's notes are more like stories. This is important, Tobin. Captain Reed lost something precious."

Captain Reed shuffled by, sadder than a ship with no wind. "My lucky sea glass," he sighed. "Gone!"

Tobin's whiskers twitched. "Lost? But Captain, Iorwerth's map is full of clues!"

Nell's eyes sparkled. "His notes make the journey fun. Let's go!"

Tobin led; Nell followed the map. They passed the bakery, and Tobin hummed off-key until he tucked his paws back, which did not entirely stop the humming.

"'Beware the pigeon with the discerning taste in seeds,'" Nell read by a birdbath. "'He judges footwear. Don't make eye contact if your socks are questionable.'" Tobin nervously eyed a plump pigeon. Nell nudged him. "Just keep your socks hidden."

Next, the quiet library. "'Consult the title that whispers of forgotten tides, or smells faintly of salty air.'" Tobin, with his keen mole eyes, spotted a worn spine. He nudged a book titled The Siren's Sigh with his nose. A faint sea-salt scent clung to it. As the book moved, a small smooth object fell out. Captain Reed's sea glass.

"We found it!" Tobin exclaimed.

The map's final note read: "The treasure is not always gold, but what makes the heart sing. If a bird pecks you, that's Iorwerth saying thank you for playing, and wear a hat."

With the glass safe they hurried back. Captain Reed sat by the river, looking forlorn.

"Captain! We have it!" Nell announced, holding up the glinting piece.

His face lit. "My sea glass! Thank you, my friends! How did you find it?"

"Iorwerth's map!" chirped Tobin. "His peculiar notes were half the treasure."

Captain Reed chuckled, booming laugh returning. "Ah, Iorwerth. His maps are about the journey. He made the search an adventure — to distract me, and to remind me of the good things. He knew funny observations would cheer me up." He held the glass.

Nell smiled at Tobin. "He was right, wasn't he? Friends, shared laughter. And maybe eccentric mapmakers."

As the sun dipped, they sat with the Captain. The bakery's sweet scent lingered; the river giggled. Iorwerth's notes had led them to the sea glass. Tobin did not file the afternoon under Friendship, Kindness, and Shared Joy. He wondered whether the next map would hide a biscuit in the library, and whether the pigeon would forgive his socks if he wore a hat, as instructed.
